name: Sev Usal
steps: Soak white peas overnight, drain and simmer in fresh water until soft but intact, roughly 40–60 minutes. Reserve 350 ml cooking liquid.
Heat oil in a broad pan, toast cumin, soften half the chopped onion with ginger and garlic, then add tomato, chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric and salt.
Cook the masala 7–8 minutes until the tomato breaks down. Add cooked peas and reserved liquid and simmer 10 minutes into a spicy spoonable usal; lightly mash a few peas to thicken.
Divide hot usal among four bowls. Add remaining raw onion, fresh coriander and a generous layer of fine sev only just before serving so the topping remains crisp.
Serve with lemon wedges and soft pav, allowing each person to squeeze lemon to taste. Keep the peas visible rather than blending the curry smooth.
tips: Add sev at the last moment or it dissolves into the hot pea gravy.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
